title: Elementary distinguished squares are universal algebraic-space pushouts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $Y,Z,V,W$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $b:V\hookrightarrow Y$ identifies $V$ with an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $a:Z\to Y$ is etale in the chartwise sense [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism], and $W=Z\times_YV$, with its projection maps [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Suppose $Z\times_YT\to T$ is an isomorphism, where $T\hookrightarrow Y$ is the reduced closed subspace supported on $|Y|\setminus|V|$, using the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology, lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]; a closed subspace means a representable map that is a closed immersion on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then this square is a pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$: for every algebraic space $H/S$, compatible maps $Z\to H$ and $V\to H$ agreeing on $W$ factor uniquely through $Y$. For every morphism $t:Y'\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, put $Z'=Z\times_YY'$, $V'=V\times_YY'$ and $W'=W\times_YY'$. The resulting square has $V'\hookrightarrow Y'$ open, $Z'\to Y'$ chartwise etale, $W'=Z'\times_{Y'}V'$, and $Z'\times_{Y'}T'\to T'$ an isomorphism for the reduced closed complement $T'$ of $V'$ in $Y'$. This base-changed square is also a pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$. No flatness, quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed on $t$ or on $a$.

source.place: Tag 0DVI (lemma-elementary-distinguished-square-pushout); base change is spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GN (lemma-make-more-elementary-distinguished-squares), parts (2) and (3).

proof.text: First $|V|\cup\operatorname{im}|a|=|Y|$: a field-valued point of $Y$ outside $V$ factors through $T$ by lem-sfb-space-reduced-map-closed-factorization (a field is reduced), and lifts to $Z$ since $Z\times_YT\simeq T$. The point and open-subspace calculus identifies the inverse image of $|V|$ with $|Z\times_YV|$. Put $D=Z\times_YZ$ and $E=D\times_YV\simeq W\times_VW$. The diagonal $\Delta:Z\to D$ is an open subspace: apply lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph to $\operatorname{id}_Z:Z\to Z$ over $Y$, using that $a$ is chartwise etale. Also $E\subseteq D$ is open by the scheme-test definition of an open subspace. Every field-valued point of $D$ outside $E$ maps into $|T|$, hence factors over $T$ by the same reduced-source factorization. Its two $Z$-coordinates then coincide because $Z\times_YT\to T$ is an isomorphism. It therefore belongs to $\Delta$. Consequently the open subspaces $\Delta$ and $E$ cover $D$, by lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus. This does not require the diagonal to be closed.

Let $H/S$ be an algebraic space, and let $g:Z\to H$, $h:V\to H$ agree on $W$. The maps $g\operatorname{pr}_1,g\operatorname{pr}_2:D\to H$ agree on $\Delta$, since both diagonal projections are the identity. On $E=W\times_VW$ each map equals $h$ composed with the common projection to $V$, by the assumed equality on $W$. For every scheme test $Q\to D$, the inverse images of $\Delta,E$ form an open cover of $Q$. Open immersions of schemes are etale by lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by def-weil-etale-morphism; this cover is fppf by def-pc-fppf-site. The uniqueness part of the fppf sheaf condition for $H$ proves equality on $Q$. Since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations on scheme tests, $g\operatorname{pr}_1=g\operatorname{pr}_2$ on $D$.

The open inclusion $V\to Y$ is chartwise etale by lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests. Thus $\{V\to Y,Z\to Y\}$ is an etale covering by Step 1 and lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence. For any scheme $R$ and $\xi:h_R\to Y$, let $V_R=R\times_YV$ and $Z_R=R\times_YZ$. Here $V_R$ is a scheme open in $R$ by the definition of open subspace. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $A\to Z_R$, available by def-trf-algebraic-space. Chartwise etale permanence shows that the composite $A\to R$ is representable etale: base change first gives $Z_R\to R$ chartwise etale and composition with its scheme chart gives the assertion. The pair $\{V_R\to R,A\to R\}$ is jointly surjective by base change and composition of etale coverings (replace the member $Z_R$ by its atlas). Both arrows are etale scheme morphisms, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. It is therefore an fppf covering of $R$, without any quasi-compactness assumption.

On the covering of Step 3 prescribe $h$ on $V_R$ and $g$ composed with $A\to Z$ on $A$. These sections of $H$ agree on every pairwise overlap: on $V_R\times_RA$ and $A\times_RV_R$ both maps factor through $W$ and the assumed compatibility applies; on $A\times_RA$ their map to $D$ allows Step 2 to apply; the $V_R$ self-overlap is immediate because $V_R\to R$ is a monomorphism. The fppf sheaf condition produces a unique section $k_R(\xi)\in H(R)$. Choosing a different atlas gives the same section: restrict to the pairwise fibre products of the two covers over $R$, where the same three overlap calculations compare the prescribed sections, and use sheaf uniqueness. If $R'\to R$, the restrictions of $k_R(\xi)$ and the section constructed for $\xi|_{R'}$ likewise agree on the common refinement of their covers, so are equal. Thus $\xi\mapsto k_R(\xi)$ defines a natural transformation $Y\to H$, hence an $S$-morphism. It restricts to $g$ and $h$ by its defining local values. Any other such morphism has these same values on every covering of Step 3 and is equal to it by sheaf uniqueness. This proves the original square's pushout property.

Now let $t:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Fibre-product associativity gives $W'\simeq Z'\times_{Y'}V'$, and the scheme-test definition shows that $V'\to Y'$ is open. Chartwise etale permanence gives that $Z'\to Y'$ is chartwise etale. Let $T'\hookrightarrow Y'$ be the reduced closed complement of $V'$, supplied by lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support. That same node says that $T\times_YY'\hookrightarrow Y'$ has underlying point space $|t|^{-1}(|T|)$, even if it is not reduced. The point and open-subspace calculus gives $|V'|=|t|^{-1}(|V|)$, so $|t|(|T'|)\subseteq|T|$. Since $T'$ is reduced, lem-sfb-space-reduced-map-closed-factorization yields a unique map $T'\to T$ over $Y$. Base-changing the given isomorphism $Z\times_YT\simeq T$ along this map gives $Z'\times_{Y'}T'\simeq Z\times_YT'\simeq T'$. This proves all the distinguished-square hypotheses for the primed square; it does not assert $T'=T\times_YY'$.

source.place: Tag 08GN (lemma-make-more-elementary-distinguished-squares), part (2); omitted proof expanded using Tag 03JJ (lemma-map-into-reduction) in spaces-properties.tex.

proof.text: Apply Steps 1--4 with $(Y,Z,V,W)$ replaced by $(Y',Z',V',W')$, using the hypotheses just verified. For every algebraic space $H/S$ the primed compatible maps factor uniquely through $Y'$, so the base-changed square is a pushout. The argument used only openness, chartwise etaleness, and the complement isomorphism, and imposed no further condition on $t$ or $a$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q50-bd7ee697d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item and all six steps, every cited statement, and Stacks 0DVI (spaces-pushouts.tex l.1507-1544), the definition of an elementary distinguished square and 08GN (spaces-perfect.tex l.1296-1343, where the proof is omitted). The statement is unchanged from base apart from removing doubled backslashes, and it matches the definition plus 0DVI and 08GN(2). Step 1: a field point outside V factors through the reduced T (reduced-map-closed-factorization) and lifts to Z. The diagonal of Z x_Y Z is open by etale-open-graph applied to id_Z over Y. A point outside E maps into T, so its two Z-coordinates coincide through Z x_Y T = T. Step 2: the diagonal and E give an open fppf cover of every scheme test, and the sheaf uniqueness for H applies. Steps 3-4: V_R together with a scheme atlas A of Z_R is an fppf cover; it is chartwise etale and jointly surjective by the permanence lemma, and a need not be representable. Gluing on the overlaps uses W, step 2 and the fact that V_R -> R is a monomorphism; atlas independence, naturality and uniqueness are written out. This is 0DVI on scheme tests. Step 5 correctly supplies the omitted 08GN(2) proof: |T'| = |t|^-1|T|, the reduced T' maps to T, and Z' x T' = (Z x_Y T) x_T T' = T'. It does not claim T' = T x_Y Y', which is right (the k[eps] example). Edge cases checked: V=Y, V empty, Z empty, nonseparated a. No new nodes. Duplicate search (rg -L for 0DVI/08GN/elementary distinguished): lem-per-open-separated-etale-pushout states the 0DVJ construction, and lem-sfb-space-distinguished-derived-gluing states 08HB with 08GN(2) only as an embedded clause; neither duplicates the item. There is no cycle: the item is not in its own proof and statement closure. Batch 5: four of the listed citations reach sec-trace-formula only through the general definition def-trf-algebraic-space, which is already a stmt_dep of the item. lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence is a generic permanence lemma for etale maps of algebraic spaces, not a step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality. I accept all of them. I accept as tool_uses the generic sfb, a1 and trf algebraic-space lemmas. The worker listed tool_uses inside split_report; the content is correct, so I left it unchanged. No fixes.
